name: lib/disk
description: Block devices and the file systems on them: the disk and volume abstractions and their cache, FAT, ISO 9660, the old Oberon file system, partitions, a RAM volume, and file systems reached over a network.
residual: Written 2026-08-24 out of the unclaimed half of source/: not one of these modules was named by any package, and every one of them compiles against the headless payload -- the failures measured on the way were all siblings of this same family being absent, not host trouble.

Partitions and PartitionsLib are marked graphical: they paint a partition map through WMGraphics -- and they take three neighbours with them, because DiskBenchmark, DiskTests and FATScavenger all read the partition table through PartitionsLib. That is the whole reason those three are out of the payload; the check named them one by one, which is what it is for. The editor above them (PartitionEditor, WMPartitions) is an application and stays in packages/apps.

RelativeFileSystem, RfsFS + RfsConnection + RfsClientProxy and TFTPFS are file systems whose transport is a network, which is why this package requires std/net. Their subject is still a file system, so they are here rather than there.
WinDisks and WinFS are the Windows twins, in the same package as their Unix counterparts.
DiskBenchmark and DiskTests are this package's own measuring tools: commands, not library, but they belong to nothing else.
IsoImages (make a bootable ISO), VirtualDisks (a disk in a file) and BootManager entered 2026-08-24: all three are about a block device that is not a physical one.

Moved out of std/ 2026-08-27 by the Rust border (docs/STDLIB.md): the standard library holds what packages talk to each other through; this is a leaf that ob get can deliver. Sources still live in source/ -- only the classification moved. `headless` false keeps it out of the SDK payload.
